provenance.quote: Plain radiograph showing multiple intrapulmonary cavities and right hilar opacity. Note the dilated trachea.
Lateral view confirms the intrapulmonary location of the cavities as well as right basal airspace shadowing.
Dilated main left bronchus and bronchus intermedius. Multiple intrapulmonary cavities which connect to the bronchial tree.
Few of the cavities containing air/fluid levels.
Note the relative apical and peripheral sparing.

PA chest radiograph demonstrates a bulky mediastinal mass with a hilum-overlay sign suggesting either an anterior or posterior location. There are also added hazy densities overlying the lower zones and bibasal pleural effusions.

Lateral projection confirms  the anterior location of the mediatinal mass. Sternotomy wires are noted consistent with the known prior coronary arterial bypass surgery. Bibasal pleural effusions are also present.

Extensive right upper lobe consolidation, with bulging of the horizontal fissure.
Progression of the necrotizing infection produced abscess as shown in the chest X-ray 2 weeks later.
